title_en: Several Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on the Development of Maritime Trial Work
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Several Opinions on the Development of Maritime Adjudication Work

Fa Fa [2006] No. 27

Maritime adjudication is an important component of the people's courts' trial work. In November 1984, the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress adopted the "Decision on Establishing Maritime Courts in Coastal Port Cities," which for the first time clarified the legal status of maritime courts. Pursuant to this Decision, the Supreme People's Court successively established ten maritime courts dedicated to the adjudication of maritime and maritime commercial disputes in Dalian, Tianjin, Qingdao, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Wuhan, Haikou, Xiamen, Ningbo, and Beihai. The high people's court of the locality where the maritime court is located is responsible for hearing appeals against judgments and rulings of the maritime court within its jurisdiction and for supervising the trial work of the maritime court. The Supreme People's Court is responsible for supervising and guiding national maritime adjudication work. Thus far, our country has become the country with the most specialized maritime judicial institutions in the world.

Since their establishment, maritime courts have adhered to the principles of impartial justice and wholehearted service to the people, kept pace with the times, forged ahead with innovation, followed the laws governing maritime adjudication, continuously improved the maritime litigation system, constantly enhanced the quality and efficiency of trials, fully exercised their specialized adjudicative functions, and lawfully and impartially adjudicated a large number of maritime and maritime commercial dispute cases, providing high-quality judicial guarantees for the development of the economy, trade, and shipping industry, and offering valuable practical experience for establishing a standardized maritime adjudication system, improving maritime legislation, and researching maritime law. Currently, maritime justice has become an external window for Chinese justice, with continuously increasing international influence and credibility.

Entering the 21st century, maritime adjudication work faces unprecedented opportunities and challenges. World multipolarization and economic globalization continuously drive changes in the world pattern, effectively promoting our country's all-round, multi-level, and wide-ranging opening up. The development momentum of foreign trade and shipping is becoming stronger. The construction of international shipping centers and regional shipping centers is flourishing. The maritime economy and ocean economy will occupy an even more important position in our national economy, and the demand for judicial guarantees in this field is increasingly prominent. With the rapid development of the economy, trade, and shipping industry, maritime and maritime commercial disputes are increasing, maritime legal relationships are becoming more complex, the tasks of maritime adjudication are becoming heavier, and the tests faced are becoming more severe. Strengthening maritime adjudication work is imperative.

I. Main Tasks and Guiding Principles of Maritime Adjudication Work

1. The main tasks of maritime adjudication work in the next five years are: Guided by Deng Xiaoping Theory and the important thought of "Three Represents," adhere to the Scientific Outlook on Development, firmly establish the socialist rule of law concept, in accordance with the policy of "impartial justice, wholehearted service to the people," centering on the work theme of "justice and efficiency," fully utilize the functions of maritime adjudication, follow the laws of maritime adjudication work, improve and perfect the maritime adjudication system, standardize maritime judicial conduct, enhance judicial capacity, raise judicial standards, strive to achieve professionalization of judges, comprehensively enhance the authority and credibility of our country's maritime justice, provide more powerful judicial guarantees for the development of the economy, trade, and shipping industry, and make new contributions to realizing the goals of the "Eleventh Five-Year Plan" and building a socialist harmonious society.

2. To strengthen maritime adjudication work, we must adhere to the Scientific Outlook on Development. We must adhere to proceeding from reality, strive to explore development ideas for maritime adjudication work that conform to Chinese characteristics, and at the same time adhere to opening up, fully draw from internationally accepted maritime judicial systems, maintain a broad international perspective, and fairly maintain the order of the international shipping market.

3. To strengthen maritime adjudication work, we must adhere to the socialist rule of law concept. First, firmly establish the concept of governing the country according to law, continuously establish a fair, efficient, and authoritative maritime adjudication system; second, firmly establish the concept of justice for the people, in accordance with the policy of "impartial justice, wholehearted service to the people," safeguard the fundamental interests of the people, and lawfully protect the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese and foreign parties; third, firmly establish the concept of fairness and justice, leverage the advantages of maritime courts, eliminate the influence and interference of local protectionism and departmental protectionism, and impartially adjudicate various types of maritime and maritime commercial dispute cases; fourth, firmly establish the concept of serving the overall situation, plan maritime adjudication work within the overall work of the Party and the state; fifth, firmly establish the concept of Party leadership, enhance the understanding of the significant significance of strengthening the Party's leadership over maritime adjudication work under the new situation, maintain the character of the maritime adjudication contingent being loyal to the state, loyal to the people, and loyal to the law, and create a new situation in maritime adjudication work.

II. Improve and Perfect the Maritime Adjudication System, Fully Utilize the Functions of Specialized Adjudication

4. Further rationalize the maritime judicial administrative system, based on the characteristics and laws of maritime adjudication work, strive to optimize the allocation mechanisms for trial resources such as personnel, finances, and materials. Gradually unify the existing management models and financial systems of maritime courts, laying a solid foundation for the future development of maritime courts.

5. Further perfect the specialized jurisdiction system for maritime and maritime commercial cases. The specialized jurisdiction system for maritime and maritime commercial cases is the foundation of our country's maritime adjudication system. Maritime courts shall accept cases according to law; parties shall not exclude the specialized jurisdiction of maritime courts through agreement, nor shall local people's courts exclude such jurisdiction by changing the cause of action. If a local people's court accepts a maritime or maritime commercial case in violation of legal provisions and the relevant provisions of the Supreme People's Court, as long as one party raises a jurisdictional objection, the superior people's court shall uphold it and transfer the case to the maritime court with jurisdiction for trial; if a superior people's court discovers that a local people's court has accepted a maritime or maritime commercial case, it may also revoke the acceptance ex officio. The Supreme People's Court and various high people's courts shall strengthen supervision to ensure that the legal system of specialized jurisdiction for maritime and maritime commercial cases is implemented. In 2007, the Supreme People's Court will conduct a special inspection on the specialized jurisdiction of maritime and maritime commercial cases; any cases accepted in violation of regulations shall be firmly corrected and circulated as notification.

Timely adjust the scope of case jurisdiction of maritime courts; cases concerning land-based source pollution of sea areas and navigable waters connecting to the sea shall be subject to the jurisdiction of maritime courts. We shall fully leverage the advantage of maritime courts being established across administrative regions, fully utilize professional expertise, actively support environmental protection public interest litigation, and selectively accept jurisdiction over a batch of such cases. Currently, the focus should be on accepting jurisdiction over cases concerning land-based source pollution of the Bohai Sea waters and the Yangtze River waters. At the same time, further study the jurisdiction issues of maritime administrative cases and gradually rationalize the jurisdiction of such cases.

6. Further strengthen the adjudication of second instance maritime and maritime commercial cases. Relevant high people's courts shall strengthen their maritime adjudication capacity, increase the intensity of maritime adjudication, earnestly fulfill the duties of appellate courts, accurately grasp the standard of adjudication, and ensure the quality of maritime adjudication.

7. Further perfect the maritime adjudication supervision system. Relevant high people's courts shall designate a trial division that hears maritime and maritime commercial cases to centrally handle cases concerning the jurisdiction of maritime and maritime commercial cases and cases of maritime adjudication supervision, ensuring uniformity of adjudication standards. Reform the maritime adjudication supervision system, formulate standards for filing retrial cases of maritime and maritime commercial cases and the trial procedures; a hearing system may be implemented before retrial, and a five-member collegial panel may be adopted when necessary.

8. Further perfect the collegial panel system. Maritime courts may, based on the type of case, relatively fix collegial panels to enhance the professional level of judges.

9. Further perfect the people's assessor system in maritime adjudication. Formulate provisions on the scope of application and selection of assessors, and gradually establish an expert assessor system for maritime and maritime commercial cases.

10. Further perfect the maritime enforcement system. Standardize compulsory measures such as the arrest and auction of ships during the pre-litigation, interim, and enforcement stages to maintain judicial authority.

III. Adhere to Scientific Trial Concepts, Adjudicate Maritime and Maritime Commercial Cases Openly and Impartially

11. Adhere to the principle of open trial, promoting justice through openness. All aspects of maritime and maritime commercial cases, including case filing, court sessions, and adjudication results, shall be made public to the extent required by law. All effective foreign-related maritime and maritime commercial judgments shall be published on the China Foreign-Related Commercial and Maritime Trial Website and the portal websites of each court, with all effective judgment documents to be publicly released within three years.

12. Fully respect party autonomy. Without violating legal principles and public order, litigation parties may dispose of their procedural and substantive rights to the maximum extent possible. In maritime litigation activities, without affecting the interests of third parties and public order, the litigation procedures may be simplified with the consent of both parties and recorded in the case file.

13. Earnestly implement the principle of facilitating litigation, reducing litigation costs for the parties. When arranging litigation activities, fully consider the interests of the parties and reduce unnecessary litigation burdens. Emphasize mediation work, adhere to the principle of "mediate where possible, adjudicate where appropriate, combine mediation with adjudication, and settle cases to close matters," and increase the rate of case settlement through mediation.

14. Strengthen the reasoning of judgment documents, improve their quality. Judgment documents shall comprehensively and objectively reflect the entire trial process, and accurately explain and rule on the matters requested by the parties and their procedural rights and obligations according to law. The first and second instance judgments in maritime and maritime commercial cases may refer to the reference style of judgment documents for foreign-related commercial dispute cases formulated by the Supreme People's Court.

IV. Strengthen Trial Supervision and Guidance, Unify Adjudication Standards

15. Strengthen judicial interpretation work, study the common and typical issues existing in current maritime adjudication, and provide timely guiding opinions. Formulate judicial interpretations on legal application issues such as marine insurance, delivery of goods without bills of lading, coastal and inland waterway transportation, freight forwarding, oil pollution damage compensation, ship collision, and the procedure for the fund for limitation of liability for maritime claims, to unify adjudication standards.

16. Strengthen guidance on trial practice, improve trial standards. Relevant high people's courts and maritime courts shall promptly study relevant issues in maritime adjudication, summarize the experiences of the courts of two instances in trial practice, and ensure that all cases concluded within their jurisdiction meet the requirements of judicial uniformity.

17. Strengthen case evaluation work. Establish a case evaluation system for maritime and maritime commercial cases. The Supreme People's Court shall conduct case evaluations from time to time and, at appropriate times, organize mutual evaluations among maritime courts and relevant high people's courts, promptly identify problems existing in trial work, and promote continuous improvement in trial quality.

18. Strengthen professional exchange in trial practice. Through periodic seminars on trial practice and other means, discuss and summarize hot and difficult issues existing in maritime adjudication, to unify understanding, enhance judicial capacity, and at the same time lay the groundwork for the Supreme People's Court to issue relevant judicial interpretations and judicial interpretation documents.

19. Strengthen the guiding role of typical cases. Relevant high people's courts shall select some typical cases and submit them to the Supreme People's Court, which will select and compile them, regularly editing and distributing them. Starting in 2007, the Supreme People's Court will compile and issue one to two volumes of selected cases each year to guide maritime adjudication work.

V. Standardize Litigation Activities, Ensure Procedural Justice

20. Standardize litigation procedures. Further improve the maritime litigation guidance system, risk warning system, case hearing scheduling system, extension of trial period reason notification system, and other systems, to avoid situations where parties have no recourse or cases are filed in violation of regulations; further standardize trial activities, strengthen procedures such as party burden of proof, cross-examination, and evidence exchange; further standardize maritime enforcement activities, disclose all aspects of enforcement, achieving standardized enforcement according to law and clean and civilized enforcement.

21. Standardize the application of summary procedures. Maritime courts may try maritime and maritime commercial cases with clear facts, explicit rights and obligations, and minor disputes according to the summary procedures stipulated in the Civil Procedure Law. In 2007, the Supreme People's Court will formulate specific provisions on summary procedures for maritime and maritime commercial cases, clarifying the scope of application of summary procedures, litigation procedures, and the preparation of judgment documents.

22. Strengthen the standardized construction of detached tribunals. Relevant high people's courts shall incorporate the work of maritime courts' detached tribunals into the management scope of people's tribunals, addressing issues such as construction and funding guarantees. Based on the needs of maritime adjudication, standardize the establishment of detached tribunals, strengthen personnel management of detached tribunals, unify work rules, strictly control trial procedures, and ensure case quality. In 2007, the Supreme People's Court will conduct spot checks on various tasks of maritime courts' detached tribunals, guiding relevant high people's courts and maritime courts to solve difficulties and problems existing in the work of detached tribunals.

23. Strictly standardize the fee collection standards for maritime litigation. Maritime courts and appellate high people's courts shall strictly follow legal provisions and the relevant provisions of the Supreme People's Court, making public all fee items and fee standards. Strengthen supervision over fee collection links such as case filing, pre-litigation and interim arrest and auction of ships, and enforcement, to prevent the occurrence of improper fee collection. For fee items and standards that need unification in practice, corresponding legal documents shall be formulated based on extensive solicitation of opinions, so that maritime litigation fees have legal basis and verifiable records.

VI. Strengthen Trial Management, Improve Work Quality and Efficiency

24. Strengthen trial process management, trial quality management, and trial organization operation management, strictly implement the responsibility system, ensuring clear powers and responsibilities. Improve the operational mechanisms for each major link of maritime justice, enhance coordination and cooperation among internal institutions of maritime courts, making the entire trial activity more scientific and standardized, more streamlined and economical, and more practical and effective.

25. Strengthen the application of information technology, increase the technological content of trial work. Gradually promote the digitization of trial records, using audio and video recording to synchronously record the entire trial process, improving the quality and efficiency of court sessions. Establish electronic databases of litigation archives, perform electronic data processing on judgment documents of concluded cases since the establishment of the court, facilitating preservation and retrieval.

26. Strengthen the communication of trial information, ensuring smooth flow of trial information among maritime courts and between maritime courts and superior courts. Timely report and file to the Supreme People's Court trial information concerning the arrest and auction of foreign ships by maritime courts and major cases.

27. Strengthen external publicity work. Each maritime court shall establish a spokesperson system to uniformly release major work deployments and important measures, trial information on various major and important cases, and cases of social concern, ensuring the public's right to know. Fully utilize the foreign-related commercial and maritime trial website to publicize maritime adjudication work, continuously enhance the transparency of maritime adjudication work, and continuously expand the influence of maritime adjudication.

VII. Strengthen Team Building, Take the Lead in Achieving Professionalization of Judges

28. Deeply carry out education on the socialist rule of law concept, adhere to the policy of "impartial justice, wholehearted service to the people," educate judges to establish correct worldviews, outlooks on life, and values, adhere to the "Eight Honors and Eight Disgraces," and strengthen ideals and beliefs.

29. Enhance judicial capacity building, improve the judicial level of maritime judges. Maritime judges must not only be proficient in law but also familiar with navigation technical knowledge; not only proficient in maritime and maritime commercial law but also proficient in ordinary civil and commercial law. Continuously improve judges' abilities to preside over court sessions, conduct judicial mediation, apply the law, and reason in judgment documents, vigorously cultivate expert-type professional judges who understand law, economics, trade, shipping, and foreign languages.

30. Strengthen the professional training of maritime judges. The Supreme People's Court is responsible for organizing one to two training sessions for maritime judges each year. Maritime courts and appellate high people's courts shall also periodically organize training for maritime judges. The training content mainly includes three aspects: young maritime judges studying in relevant practical departments, basic civil and commercial law training, and professional skills training, continuously achieving knowledge updates.

31. Establish a scientific management model for the maritime judge team. Relevant high people's courts shall earnestly exercise their duties of cadre management and supervision over maritime judges, formulate long-term plans for the construction of the maritime judge team. To broaden the horizons of maritime judges, relevant high people's courts shall select maritime judges for exchange to local people's courts or superior courts. Strengthen the construction of the leadership team of maritime courts, select and equip strong "first persons in charge." Include the leading cadres of maritime courts in the sequence of leading cadres of ordinary intermediate people's courts for cultivation, promotion, and exchange use, promoting the healthy development of maritime courts.

VIII. Strengthen Cooperation and Exchange, Expand International Influence

32. Organize maritime judges to participate in Chinese delegations participating in the drafting and revision of relevant international maritime conventions. Learn from and draw on the experiences and practices of other countries' maritime justice, improving our country's maritime legislation and judicial levels.

33. Select outstanding judges for training and visits to countries with relatively mature maritime legal systems, broadening judges' international perspectives. Training methods may include regular training at renowned foreign universities, or inviting internationally renowned maritime legal experts and maritime judges to the country, organizing judges for centralized domestic training. Through various forms of training, help judges promptly grasp the development trends of the international shipping market and understand the latest developments in international maritime law.

34. Hold international maritime judicial forums to understand the dynamics and information of maritime justice in various countries, while simultaneously introducing China's maritime judicial system to the world, expanding the international influence of our country's maritime adjudication.

IX. Strengthen Leadership, Promote the Comprehensive and Sustainable Development of Maritime Adjudication Work

35. To achieve the comprehensive development of maritime adjudication work, leadership is key. Relevant high people's courts shall strengthen supervision and guidance over maritime courts, list the development of maritime adjudication as an important work content, study the basic construction, team building, and problems existing in maritime adjudication work of their subordinate maritime courts, and promptly adopt practical and feasible measures to solve them. Maritime courts shall promptly report to superior courts on the situation of various tasks, including difficulties and existing problems, and consciously accept the supervision and guidance of superior courts. Maritime courts and appellate high people's courts shall stand at a strategic height, in accordance with the requirements of the Supreme People's Court, invigorate their spirits, work diligently, forge ahead with innovation, strive to explore new ideas for the development of maritime adjudication, and create a new situation in maritime adjudication work.

November 9, 2006
